quest.title: Lost and Inherited
quest.description: Colter tells you stories of the Spina di Rosula's past. After a rest, it is time to head off to the Court of Fontaine.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x475, Mora x34075, Unknown Item #373437 x1, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

talks.objective: Go to the Court of Fontaine to collect the goods

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hey there, Ludivine? How's business lately?

dialogues.speaker: Ludivine
dialogues.text: Ah, the Demoiselle of Spina di Rosula! I must say, your generous patronage is the one thing keeping me from going bankrupt.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Haha, nonsense, we all know what a talented businesswoman you are. Oh, and don't forget, she's the Boss now.

dialogues.speaker: Ludivine
dialogues.text: My mistake, my mistake. I just got so used to calling her Demoiselle.

dialogues.speaker: Ludivine
dialogues.text: Are you here for the uniform?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yup. I forgot to drop by earlier when I was running errands around here.

dialogues.speaker: Ludivine
dialogues.text: Haha, I didn't expect Demoiselle to come and pick it up in person. It's just a uniform, after all. Any of your folks could have come instead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Navia's always liked to take even small things seriously!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hey, that's not the only reason I'm here! We mostly just needed a walk to clear our heads.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: There are few things more uplifting than taking the first step on a new journey.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Haha, Boss has got a point. Going on a trip with friends is always better than staying cooped up at home.

dialogues.speaker: Ludivine
dialogues.text: Very well... Please wait here while I retrieve the uniform for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, can someone remind Paimon again why Adele wants to join the Spina?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hehe, she hasn't given me any concrete reasons. All she says is that she really looks up to me.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: After we cleared her father's name, she became a lot more cheerful and outgoing. It's probably because she now knows for sure that her father was never a bad person.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: She said she used to be terrified of Papa, so as a result, she found all the rest of the Spina super scary as well.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: But the Spina is very different now. She mustered up the courage to talk to me, and felt like I could really understand her.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The two of you have contended with similar circumstances.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Yeah, you could say that. By uncovering the truth about the case, I was able to give her closure at the same time.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: She said that she wanted to become someone like me — someone who could lend a hand to others, instead of standing still and waiting for others to help her.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: From the sound of it, she'll be a wonderful addition to the Spina.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I think so too, but for now, let's focus on giving her a great atmosphere to grow and thrive. She can commit to us once she's older, and can really make that decision for herself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So I wasn't just hearing things.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is something up, Traveler?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? T—Tailing? Paimon's coming!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I'll go check it out too! Colter, please hold on to this for me!

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: A—Alright!

talks.objective: Catch up with the people following you

dialogues.speaker: Martinat
dialogues.text: Tch. We knew you were going to be difficult.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Huh. Seems like if we want them to talk, we're gonna need to teach them a lesson first.

dialogues.speaker: Martinat
dialogues.text: Brothers, there's no need to skulk in the dark anymore! Let's take them out!

talks.objective: Talk to Martinat and the others

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Now talk. Who are you, and why were you tailing us?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't think we'll let you off easy if you keep silent!

choices.text: Recognize your situation, and don't entertain any fantasies of escape.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: How did it go, Boss? Are any of you hurt?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Heh, if you thought they stood any chance against us, you were sorely mistaken.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Anyway, stop playing tough and start talking. There won't be any room for negotiation once the Maison Gardiennage gets involved.

response.speaker: Martinat
response.text: We... were looking to get vengeance on Spina di Rosula.

response.speaker: Martinat
response.text: We were discovered, and can't beat you in a fight... We admit it, we lost.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Get revenge? Wait... You're not Romeuf's followers, are you?

response.speaker: Martinat
response.text: You actually know that name...?

response.speaker: Martinat
response.text: But if you do, then surely, you should understand why we hate you so much!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I would advise you to calm down.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: Indeed. You haven't got the faintest hope of winning right now.

response.speaker: Martinat
response.text: Tch...

response.speaker: Martinat
response.text: We were out drinking when we saw Navia. We got so angry, we decided to follow you guys and look for an opportunity to really mess up your day.

response.speaker: Martinat
response.text: Too bad you guys messed up ours first.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're lying.

response.speaker: Martinat
response.text: Huh...?

choices.text: You followed us all the way here.

response.speaker: Martinat
response.text: You're pretty sharp, but so what? We didn't do anything, and now it should be pretty obvious that we can't do anything to you anyway.

response.speaker: Martinat
response.text: Seeing you like that just really ticked us off, and we let the drink go to our heads.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Listen, Callas is long dead. No matter what happened in the past, I want to be able to start things anew.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I am the current President of Spina di Rosula. If your boss wants to talk with me, I'd be happy to meet with him.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I won't press charges for your attack. That should also help demonstrate my sincerity.

response.speaker: Martinat
response.text: ...I understand, thank you. I'll let our Boss know.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But if you so much as think about pulling something like this again, I won't be so lenient next time. Understood?

response.speaker: Martinat
response.text: Alright, we get it. C'mon, let's go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, are you sure it's okay to just let them go like that, Navia?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I don't want to inherit my father's grudges, too. Moreover, when it comes to the aquabus, I don't think what my father did was entirely correct, either.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: If the other side is willing to talk, I'm happy to open the door for a reconciliation. Opportunities for new beginnings are all around us.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: I support Boss' decision as well. The concept of "an eye for an eye" is a primitive practice that has no place in today's Spina di Rosula.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yes. Plus, we already know that they're strapped for cash. If their financial situation is that dire, they don't have what it takes to challenge us, so this may be the best time to talk.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I still think we should keep an eye out for Romeuf's folks, though. If he decides to ignore the warning I gave his men...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Then we could still have a fight on our hands.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, those guys definitely didn't look like big fans of yours.

response.speaker: Colter
response.text: I'd rather things not go that far, since... Though we haven't talked to each other for years, once upon a time, we were all a part of the Spina di Rosula family.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yep, that's how I feel as well. Anyway, now that we've sent them packing, we don't have to worry about those guys anymore.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: It's getting late already, so why don't we stay the night in the Fleuve Cendre? We can head back to Poisson tomorrow.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I'll also ask someone to write Florent a letter and inform him of everything that happened here today, so he can increase security around Poisson, and be on guard against any suspicious individuals.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do we have to stay in the Fleuve Cendre again? Even the pillows there smell like seaweed...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Sorry, that's just what happens when you live near water and don't get much sunlight. Poisson's pretty much the same, though, so I've long since gotten used to it.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: We can still go out in the evening for some grilled fish and drinks, though. Bet you there'll be people singing sea shanties too! How does that sound?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that does sound pretty cool! Okay, Paimon's on board now. Let's go, Paimon wants to sing, too!

choices.text: We've got people up above and down below as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Coming back here, it really does feel like this place is starting to grow on Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If you think about it, it would be kind of weird if the Spina's base at the Court was some super luxurious building like the Palais Mermonia.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hahaha, totally! Right on the money, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Although of course, with the continued growth of the Spina, Papa wanted Poisson to eventually grow into a metropolis not unlike the Court.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: He was a very ambitious man who rarely looked behind or beneath him. For better or worse, that always made him stand out from the crowd.

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: And that's also why people hated him just as much as they loved him.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Alright, why don't you wait for me at the restaurant? I'll go do some prep, and I'll get someone to tidy up your room while I'm at it.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: You can use the same room as last time. You still remember the room number, yeah?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep yep! Kinda hard to forget when there are only so many rooms here after all.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Oho, did I just hear someone taking a dig at Fleuve Cendre? I'll tell my guys to stuff your pillows full of actual seaweed right now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's sorry! Please have mercy, Navia! If you do that, then Paimon really won't be able to sleep at all!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hahaha, I was just kidding. Be on your way, now.

talks.objective: Sit inside and wait for the banquet to begin

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You enjoy a fantastic meal as well as a wonderful performance. The boisterous night begins to slip away before you know it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As things slowly die down, you return to your room with Paimon, but you soon hear a knock at the door...

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hello? Are you asleep yet?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: No, not at all. I just figured that since we don't get to enjoy nights like these very often, we should try to enjoy it to the fullest.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Wanna go fishing? I've got some rods and lures ready.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so that's the "prep" you were talking about! Sure, we'll come!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hehe, hopefully I didn't wake you or anything.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Don't worry, you don't have to do any actual fishing if you're too tired.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Just think of it as keeping me company. How does that sound?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Okay, let's go. To the fishing spot!

choices.text: Since the invitation is coming from you...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hehe, I knew it, you really are my best partner!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How can you call this fishing when you're using a fully automatic rod!?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hmm? What's the problem? Lots of people in Poisson use rods like these.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... But shouldn't fishing be all about... You know, attentively watching the float, and then excitedly reeling in the catch when you've finally hooked something?

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: #Well, that's one way to enjoy fishing! What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: I like Paimon's method. Manual all the way.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Then let's try regular rods next time. We can have a real fishing competition!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Honestly, Paimon's mainly shocked at how much energy you still have at this hour. Usually, by this time of night, it's a struggle for Paimon to even keep her eyes open!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Eh, it might just be something that runs in my family.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's a thing?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Hehe, I'm sure you'd just get even sleepier if I delved more deeply into it. Anyway, I was just thinking about how grateful I am to my mother, as well as the rest of the Spina.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Your mother?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: My father always had a lot of unrealistic expectations for me, but the more that he tried to get me to become like him, the less I wanted to listen to what he had to say.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: My mother never had those kinds of expectations, though. I've heard that she had only one wish for me, which was that I would have a happy and secure childhood.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: All the members of the Spina greatly respected her wish, so no matter what I did as a child, they were happy to humor me.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Can you imagine? Whenever my father wanted to scold me for something I'd done, everyone would form up into two rows, and just stand silently and listen to him rant. Melus and Silver were always there, too.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: No matter what Papa yelled, nobody else would say a word. Eventually, Papa must have recognized scolding me over trivial matters was pointless, because he eventually stopped getting on my case so often.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon would've never guessed...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Yeah... looking back on it now as an adult, I can hardly believe how patient and kind everyone was.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: When I was young, I often thought that I could do whatever I wanted, because there'd always be someone there to clean up after me.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: But once, I saw Melus come back wounded. He wouldn't tell me how he'd been injured, but I could tell that it had something to do with me.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: I learned then that there's always a cost to making a mistake. The more you care about those around you, the more you should care about doing the right thing to the best of your abilities.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Because if you do falter, there will inevitably come a time when you'll have to face the consequences. And when that time comes, those most precious to you really will throw themselves in front of you, and pay the price for your mistakes...

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Sorry, sorry, I shouldn't have brought that up. I wasn't planning to talk about sad things tonight.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Basically, I was just saying that the nurturing atmosphere of the Spina must have been my mother's legacy, rather than my father's.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: And if that's the only way that I can continue to feel her love, then I'd like to pass that warmth on.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that why you let those guys go today?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Mhm, although maybe there's a part of not wanting to repeat the mistakes of the past. I want to be reasonable, at least.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}, look! I think you've got something on the line!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why isn't the rod automatically reeling it in?

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: There must be something wrong with how I installed the mechanism. It was my first time putting one of those rods together!

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: We can't let it get away! C'mon, you two, let's catch it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y—You want Paimon to help too!?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After some time, you finally manage to reel in the prize catch together.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: For the rest of the night, your rod continues to rack up catch after catch, while for some reason, Navia can't seem to hook a single fish.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Navia is quite upset about her bad luck, but it's only when you begin to head back that Paimon discovers the real reason to the mystery of why she didn't get a single bite.

choices.text: It must still be really hard for you.

response.speaker: Navia
response.text: Haha, that's how I feel as well. To me, I'm happy as long as I catch some fish.

talks.objective: Return to the Fleuve Cendre to rest

dialogues.speaker: Martinat
dialogues.text: Stop wasting time. The Boss ain't gonna wait all day.

dialogues.speaker: Martinat
dialogues.text: We'll go ahead with the operation tomorrow. Do with that information as you wish.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Heh, well your rod was missing a part too, so... I guess that makes it fair.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, if we're just talking about the number of missing parts, sure... *yawn* Ugh, never mind, Paimon really can't keep her eyes open anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Hahaha, alright, go to bed! I had a great time today.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you tomorrow, Navia.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Mhm, see you tomorrow!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: So, how was last night? Did you get a good night's sleep?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon dreamt that she danced with the sea stars... So you could say it was stellar, get it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...And just where did you get that from...?

dialogues.speaker: Colter
dialogues.text: Haha, I didn't know you had such a great sense of humor.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: See, this guy gets it!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's head out. I'll arrange for a boat to take us back to Poisson. I'm sure Adele will be happy to see you two again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon hopes she'll really appreciate your gift!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I hope so too.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: All set? Let's move out, then.

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: I asked some old acquaintances in town to make Adele's uniform, so we should be able to pick it up right away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon saw them too! They headed up!

dialogues.speaker: Navia
dialogues.text: Stop right there!
